transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… things have been falling apart since the foreclosure notices started coming. I’m not handling it well. I’ve been crying in my truck before work, getting jumpy when the phone rings, snapping at the apprentices… and I’ve been making mistakes in the repair bay I wouldn’t normally make.
Have you lost interest in things you usually enjoy, like hobbies or spending time with family?

Yeah… I guess I have. I stopped going to the things I used to keep up with — church volunteering, my fitness class, the truck-club stuff. And at work they took me out of the high-risk repair bay, so… it’s affecting things.
Have you been feeling tired or lacking energy most days, even when you haven’t been doing much?
I don’t know… I mean, I’m tired some days, sure, but I haven’t really been paying attention to it like that.
Have you been feeling down or in a low mood most days, even when there’s nothing specific happening to cause it?

Yeah… since the foreclosure notices started, mostly. It’s like I’m barely holding it together. I end up crying before work sometimes, sitting in my truck, and I’m on edge all the time. It’s not really out of nowhere, I guess… it’s tied to that.
Do your symptoms, like feeling down or on edge, only happen when you're dealing with the foreclosure stress, or do they stick around even when nothing specific is going on?

It’s mostly when that foreclosure stuff is hanging over me, yeah. Since those notices started, I feel like I’m… coming apart. Crying in my truck before work, getting jumpy when the phone rings. I’ve been short with the apprentices, too, and making mistakes in the bay I wouldn’t normally make.
Even when you're not thinking about the foreclosure or related stress, do you still find yourself feeling down, anxious, or struggling to function?

Not really separate from it, no. Ever since those notices started coming, I just feel like I’m coming apart… crying in my truck before work, jumping when the phone rings. And it’s affecting work too—I’m snapping at the apprentices and making dumb mistakes in the bay I wouldn’t normally make.
When you’re not dealing with the foreclosure stress or reminders of it, do you still feel anxious, down, or have trouble functioning?

Not really… it’s all kind of tied to that. Since those notices started coming, I just feel like I’m coming apart. I cry in my truck before work, jump when the phone rings… and I’ve been snapping at the apprentices, making mistakes in the bay I wouldn’t normally make.
